title: Flow Regulator: SLO-aware simulator and auto-revert protocol for batching & KV cache tuning
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: build a flow regulator subsystem that 1) simulates the impact of proposed batching and KV-prefetch configs against production-like traffic, 2) applies changes via a staged canary that enforces latency/throughput SLOs, and 3) automatically reverts when anomaly detectors trigger. This ticket covers the simulator harness, the limiter/circuit state machine, SLO gates for routing and canarying, and the auto-revert protocol integrated into the rollout controller.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Simulator can replay 3 types of traffic traces (steady, spiky, long-tail) and show predicted p50/p95/p99 latency and throughput changes for a candidate config. 2) Rollout controller rejects/halts apply if simulated regressions exceed thresholds or if live canary violates SLO gates for two consecutive buckets. 3) Auto-revert triggers within 60s of violation and restores previous config with accompanied audit log and incident ticket. 4) End-to-end e2e test that flips a synthetic anomaly and verifies revert + alerting flows.
implementation_notes: Simulator: lightweight traffic replay built on existing trace-exporter; supports request-to-sequence mapping and synthetic KV-hit/miss modeling. Cost model uses token-per-op and GPU-occupancy estimator. Anomaly detector: hybrid EWMA + MAD on per-route p95 and queue length; configurable sensitivity by route. Limiter/circuit: state machine (Closed -> Probe -> Throttled -> Open) driven by rolling-window metrics and hysteresis timers. SLO-aware routing: requests tagged with tier; canary fraction controlled by SafeStepper algorithm (exponential ramp with decay on noise). Auto-revert: rollback API call that sets previous config and initiates a fast-canary verification; audit entry emitted to logs/console and create incident via ops webhook. Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, queue depth, batches-per-second, tokens/sec, GPU util, kw-hit-rate. Observability: events emitted to console-rollouts, and a dedicated dashboard snapshot for canaries.
testing_plan: 1) Unit tests for state machine transitions and threshold evaluation. 2) Simulator regression tests using recorded traces from two customers (anonymized) and synthetic spike traces. 3) Integration test: create canary with tuned batch/cache config in staging cluster, inject latencies, verify SLO gate and auto-revert. 4) Chaos test: flakey GPU and KV backend failures to validate graceful fallback. 5) Load test: verify scale behavior under high QPS.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: internal staging only (team opt-in) for 1 week. Stage 2: 5% production traffic shadow mode for two days with simulator feedback only. Stage 3: 1% live canary with strict SLO gates for 24h. Stage 4: progressive stepper to 10% then 50% with automatic halt on anomaly. Final: global apply after 7 days of stable metrics. All stages create automated snapshots and a revert trigger that can flip within 60s.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: false positives from anomaly detector causing unnecessary reverts. Mitigation: dual-detector voting (EWMA + seasonal MAD) and minimum sample-size guard. Risk: simulator prediction drift vs real infra. Mitigation: continuous calibration using recent 72h sliding window of real canary results. Risk: revert thrashing under flapping infra. Mitigation: backoff timer and max-reverts-per-hour limit.
